- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), often peaking 1–2 days too early.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods, particularly when prices drop below 70–72.
- Tends to ignore recent downward momentum in the 30-day history, especially when the last 5–7 days show declining trends.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts often lag behind true price corrections by 1–3 days.
- When true outcome is below 70, model frequently fails to recognize the trend and continues to forecast higher values.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values in the first 10 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts downward — but often too late or too much.
- When history includes a recent spike followed by a drop, model often forecasts a prolonged high, ignoring the correction phase.
